projects.title: Project ATLAS
projects.summary: Building an evidence-grounded research workspace: from a research question to inspectable sources, reproducible experiments and carefully qualified conclusions.
projects.alt: ATLAS system diagram: research brief, source library and cited records, with later research stages marked as roadmap work.
projects.body:
ATLAS is my ongoing project to make AI-assisted research inspectable. The aim is to preserve the reasoning, source material and experimental record behind a conclusion, so the work can be examined and reproduced.

The foundation supports durable research briefs and a responsive workspace. The next branch adds a literature library, original PDF preservation, page-level text, exact passage search and optional structured paper records. The broader autonomous research loop is still being built.

caseStudy.label: Research systems / 001
caseStudy.subtitle: Research, with an inspectable trail.
caseStudy.goal: Connect a research question to literature, structured evidence, falsifiable hypotheses and reproducible experiments—then produce conclusions that expose their evidence, uncertainty and limitations.

code.title: Keep candidate statements explicitly unverified
code.text:
class GroundedStatement(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    text: StatementText
    citations: list[PageCitation] = Field(
        min_length=1, max_length=MAX_CITATIONS_PER_STATEMENT
    )
    verification_status: Literal["UNVERIFIED"] = "UNVERIFIED"
code.note: Excerpt from the M1 branch; line breaks adjusted for readability. The schema requires citations and an explicit UNVERIFIED status. Separate validation checks quotations against stored page text.

next: Review and merge the M1 literature-library milestone.
Build the evidence graph: claims, evidence spans, support, contradiction and qualification.
Add research planning, falsifiable hypotheses and versioned experiments.
Develop statistical analysis, a research critic and a controlled iteration loop.
caseStudy.limits: No live model inference or research experiment has been validated. Current text retrieval is literal, not semantic ranking. OCR, automated experiments, statistical analysis and report generation remain future work. Saved budget fields are planning metadata, not enforced spending limits.

headings.purpose: Make the path to a conclusion inspectable.
headings.implementation: A durable foundation. A traceable library.

sections.heading: What the foundation makes possible
sections.body: A research brief stores the question, domain, constraints, datasets, budget, depth, methodology, exclusions and intended deliverable. Projects can be reopened after reload, with durable creation events and versioned database migrations.
bullets: Responsive project creation and inspection in Next.js and TypeScript.
FastAPI contracts backed by SQLite for local work and PostgreSQL for container deployment.
A typed provider boundary with explicitly configured model tiers and offline error-path tests.

sections.heading: How the literature library works
sections.body: The M1 branch preserves original PDF bytes and a server-computed SHA-256 hash. Extracted page text becomes the coordinate system for exact citations. A reader can search a phrase, inspect the matching page and trace a candidate statement back to a quotation.
bullets: Crossref imports bibliographic metadata; it does not automatically download papers.
PDF processing has explicit size, page, text and timeout limits, plus states for scans and failures.
Optional extraction records attempts and supplied usage, rejects mismatched quotations and avoids duplicate calls for a reused request identifier.

projects.title: Daymark Local
projects.summary: A local-first Windows planner, habit tracker and learning journal that connects daily intentions with a detailed record of what actually happened.
projects.alt: Daymark architecture: plan and record in the browser, persist in local SQLite, and optionally sync commitments and reports to Google.
projects.body:
Daymark brings planning, habits and learning notes into one workspace on a Windows PC. It records what was read, learned or done alongside time spent, so progress has context beyond a completed checkbox.

The app works locally without a cloud database. An optional Google connection sends commitments to Calendar and generates progress reports in Sheets. Personal records remain separate from the source repository.

caseStudy.label: Personal software / 002
caseStudy.subtitle: Plan the day. Keep the story.
caseStudy.goal: Build a practical personal workspace that joins daily planning, consistent habits, focused learning and reflection, while keeping the primary record on the user’s own computer.
caseStudy.repositoryNote: Private repository · GitHub access is required. Daymark runs locally; this page is a project overview, not the application.

headings.development: From a daily journal to a connected workspace.

code.title: Commit local changes atomically
code.note: Excerpt from the local state store, formatted for readability. A transaction commits the updated state and revision together, or rolls back when an operation fails.
code.principle: Local state commits first. Optional sync follows.

next: Keep using and refining the daily planning and journal workflows.

caseStudy.limits: Daymark is built for one Windows PC. Local reminders require the app to be running and the PC awake. Sheets is a reporting destination, not a two-way editor. Calendar changes made remotely are not merged back into local records. The build record does not independently verify a live Calendar create/edit/delete round trip or visible Windows notification delivery.

sections.heading: A daily plan with a meaningful journal
sections.body: Plan commitments on a 24-hour timeline, schedule habits and apply reusable routines. Record minutes and notes about the activity, then review daily, weekly and monthly progress.
bullets: Flexible weekday schedules, historical targets, pauses and streak rules.
Persistent focus and Pomodoro sessions with confirmed logging; breaks do not count as work.
Skill outcomes and resource links, sleep and mood check-ins, and weekly reflections.

sections.heading: Storage, recovery and optional reporting
sections.body: A Node.js server binds to the local machine and stores the primary record in SQLite. Credentials are separate, and Windows protects the Google credential file with DPAPI. Backups and restore support recovery without including credentials in JSON exports.
bullets: Local-first operation with a Windows launcher and no runtime npm dependencies.
Google desktop OAuth with PKCE; queued changes retry while the app runs.
Calendar commitments and app-managed Sheets dashboards; personal data is excluded from GitHub.
